evidence_articles.title: KTR hints at padayatra in 2027, rules out tie-up with BJP - The Hindu
evidence_articles.rephrased: **K.T. Rama Rao**, working president of the **Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS)**, stated that the party will contest the upcoming elections independently and return to power. He also hinted at a state-wid
evidence_articles.content: Hyderabad Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K.T. Rama Rao ruled out any alliance with any party in the coming elections, and also hinted at a padayatra next year to reconnect with people. Mr. Rama Rao, who was in Kyatanpally municipality on Sunday to felicitate the newly-elected members, said, “Alliances have not worked for us. We will contest alone and return to power,” and denied any tie-up with the BJP in future. He also hinted at undertaking a State-wide padayatra in 2027 focusing on public issues, as part of efforts to reconnect with the people and strengthen the party. He admitted that a gap had developed between the party and the people during its decade in power. On delimitation, Mr. Rama Rao said that the proposed increase in Assembly and Parliamentary constituencies would create new political opportunities. He maintained that if the current proportional representation is retained, there would be no objection. “If all states receive a uniform increase in seats without reducing existing share, there is no reason for concern,” he observed. Admitting shortcomings during the BRS government’s tenure, KTR said the party failed to maintain effective coordination with grassroots leaders, including cadre, sarpanches, MPTCs and mandal-level representatives. He also acknowledged that despite a large migrant workforce from north Telangana districts, the government could not formulate a comprehensive Gulf policy. He criticised the Revanth Reddy government, alleging that key welfare schemes such as Rythu Bandhu and farm loan waivers were not being implemented properly. He also flagged delays in fee reimbursement affecting students and claimed that public confidence in the government was declining. KTR criticised the allocation of funds to the Pranahita project despite objections from Maharashtra and demanded early completion of the Chennur lift irrigation scheme. On Singareni, he said that expansion of opencast mining was reducing employment opportunities and leading to worker discontent. Published - April 12, 2026 10:05 pm IST

recent_articles.title: Push for public transport exposes structural gaps - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi's** push for public transport, particularly metro rail, has prompted politicians and bureaucrats to use such systems. However, the renewed spotlight on public transit highlights a gap between policy intent and on-ground delivery.  Years of underinvestment in mass rapid transit systems have led to stalled projects like the Hyderabad Metro’s second phase and the Multi-Modal Transport System (MMTS) network. While efforts are underway to improve connectivity and funding, challenges remain, including securing approvals for expansion and procuring new train sets. The State government is also exploring a Rapid Rail Transit System (RRTS), but its suitability for urban settings remains questioned.
